source_refs.note: Steps of crystallization, printed as 15.4.1 with Figure 15.5 and the Keep in Mind box, pages 327-328.

items: Prepare a saturated solution of the substance in a suitable solvent at the temperature of the experiment.
Remove the insoluble impurities by filtering the hot saturated solution; this avoids premature crystallization on the filter paper or in the funnel stem, using a hot-water funnel if necessary.
Cool the hot filtered solution at a moderate rate so that medium-sized crystals form.
When crystallization is complete, filter the mixture of crystals and mother liquor through a Gooch crucible with a vacuum pump.

Dry the crystals in air or in an oven, the oven only if the substance does not melt or decompose at 100 degrees C. A safe, reliable method is a vacuum desiccator: the crystals are spread on a watch glass and kept in the desiccator for several hours over a drying agent such as CaCl2, silica gel or phosphorus pentoxide.

blocks.text: Coloured or resinous impurities that spoil the appearance of a product are removed by boiling the substance in the solvent with finely powdered animal charcoal and filtering hot: the coloured impurities are adsorbed on the charcoal and the decolourised substance crystallizes from the filtrate on cooling. Figure 15.5 shows the sequence: a solution of one solid with an insoluble impurity, excess solid filtered off, the hot liquid transferred to an evaporating dish and evaporated until saturated, and crystals forming on cooling.

blocks.alt: Five steps from left to right: a beaker of solution with an insoluble impurity at the bottom; filtering through a funnel and filter paper into an evaporating dish, the solid left on the paper; heating the dish on a tripod over a burner to reduce the volume until the solution is saturated; pouring the hot liquid into a dish; and crystals forming in the dish as it cools.
blocks.caption: Different steps involved in crystallization (original diagram after Figure 15.5).

blocks.text: Mention the important steps of crystallization, and say how a yellow-tinged crude sample would be decolourised.
